mainTopic: Proving that סיחון was still alive when אהרן died, so that משה's speech (after killing סיחון) came after אהרן's death; identifying the כנעני מלך ערד with סיחון; and a new challenge that the year might begin in אייר.
overview: The גמרא is proving that years counted from יציאת מצרים, and the years of kings, begin in ניסן. First it shows that סיחון was still alive when אהרן died, because the כנעני king of ערד, who is סיחון himself, attacked after hearing of אהרן's death. That makes אב and the later שבט part of the same 'fortieth year.' The גמרא then asks whether the year might begin in אייר or סיון, and rules both out from פסוקים. It cannot rule out תמוז, אב or אדר this way, so that method fails. רבי אלעזר brings a new source: 'in the second month, in the second' means the second month counted from the month a king's reign is counted from. רבינא and the גמרא test other readings of that extra word and reject them. A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן then lists all these פסוקים together. Finally, רב חסדא says non-Jewish kings count from תשרי, proving it from נחמיה. The גמרא begins to challenge that proof, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The king of ערד heard that אהרן died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the verse about the כנעני מלך ערד as showing that he attacked ישראל because אהרן died and the ענני כבוד left.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the כנעני, king of ערד, heard.' What news did he hear? He heard that אהרן had died and the ענני כבוד had left. He thought he now had permission to fight against ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that a certain king was alive and attacked ישראל right after אהרן died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say what the king 'heard.' The גמרא fills that gap: he heard about אהרן's death and the loss of the protecting clouds. This places the king's attack after אהרן's death, which means the king was still alive at that point.

keyTerms.meaning: the clouds of glory that protected ישראל in the desert

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the timeline: the king (later identified as סיחון) was alive after אהרן died. Since משה's speech came after סיחון was killed, the speech must have come after אהרן's death.

phrases.english: "And the Canaanite, king of Arad, heard"
What news did he hear?
He heard that Aaron had died,
and the clouds of glory had withdrawn,
and he thought permission was given to fight against Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier proof on the daf that משה's speech came after אהרן's death.
steps.raayaObject: That the king who fought ישראל was alive after אהרן's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כא:א, read together with the death of אהרן.

steps.title: Supporting verse read as 'they were seen'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports this from the פסוק about אהרן's death, which רבי אבהו reads as 'they were seen,' meaning ישראל became exposed without the clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'And all the congregation saw that אהרן had died.' רבי אבהו said: Do not read it as 'they saw'; read it as 'they were seen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק as support and rereads one word in it, so that the פסוק describes ישראל becoming visible and unprotected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וַיִּרְאוּ ('they saw') and וַיִּירָאוּ ('they were seen') share the same letters but can be read differently. Read as 'they were seen,' the פסוק says ישראל were exposed to their enemies once אהרן died. This matches the idea from step 1 that the clouds left.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written (a supporting verse)
do not read it as ... but rather as (a reading-based דרשה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the text is being changed. It is a דרשה that adds a second layer of meaning to the same letters.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And all the congregation saw that Aaron had died"
And Rabbi Abbahu said:
Do not read "and they saw,"
but rather "and they were seen,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second פסוק to confirm that the clouds left when אהרן died.
steps.raayaObject: That ישראל were exposed after אהרן's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כ:כט as read by רבי אבהו.

steps.title: The word כי can mean 'because'
steps.stepSummary: Following ריש לקיש, the word כי in the פסוק means 'because': ישראל were exposed because אהרן died.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows ריש לקיש, who said: the word כי is used in four meanings: 'if,' 'perhaps,' 'but,' and 'because.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how to read the word כי in the פסוק, using ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we read 'they were seen,' the word כי cannot mean 'that.' Here it means 'because' (דהא). So the פסוק says: ישראל were seen, because אהרן had died and the clouds left with him.

keyTerms.meaning: a word with several meanings in תנ"ך

phrases.english: in accordance with Reish Lakish.
For Reish Lakish said:
"Ki" is used in four meanings:
if, perhaps, but, because.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading of the פסוק from step 2 by explaining the word כי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כי has four meanings; here it means 'because.'

steps.title: The פסוק is about a כנעני king, not סיחון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק speaks about the Canaanite king of ערד, while משה's speech followed the killing of סיחון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this comparable? There the פסוק speaks about כנען; here we need סיחון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof: the king who attacked after אהרן's death seems to be a different person from סיחון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs סיחון to have been alive after אהרן died. Steps 1-3 only showed that the Canaanite king of ערד was alive then. If they are two different kings, the proof says nothing about סיחון.

keyTerms.meaning: סיחון, king of the אמורי, killed by משה

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There it is Canaan; here it is Sihon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof built in steps 1-3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that סיחון was alive after אהרן's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes a different king (כנעני מלך ערד), so it proves nothing about סיחון.

steps.title: סיחון, ערד, and כנען are one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that סיחון, ערד, and כנען are all the same king. סיחון is a nickname, כנען is his kingdom, and ערד is his real name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: He is סיחון, he is ערד, he is כנען. 'סיחון' because he was like a wild foal in the desert. 'כנען' after his kingdom. What was his name? ערד was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection with a ברייתא showing that all three names belong to one king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is explained differently: one is a nickname describing his wild nature, one is the name of his kingdom, and one is his personal name. Since the Canaanite king of ערד is סיחון, the proof works again: סיחון was alive after אהרן died.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof stands: the king who attacked after אהרן's death was סיחון, so משה's speech, given after סיחון was killed, came after אהרן's death.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סִיחוֹן, הוּא עֲרָד, הוּא כְּנַעַן.
phrases.english: He is Sihon, he is Arad, he is Canaan.
Sihon, because he resembled a foal in the desert;
Canaan, after his kingdom;
and what was his name? Arad was his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוּא סִיחוֹן, הוּא עֲרָד, הוּא כְּנַעַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identification: the two kings are actually one person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Canaanite king of ערד and סיחון were two different kings.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the same king, called by three different names.

steps.title: Second version: his real name was סיחון
steps.stepSummary: Another version reverses the names: 'ערד' is the nickname (like a wild donkey), 'כנען' is his kingdom, and סיחון is his real name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'ערד' because he was like a wild donkey in the desert. 'כנען' after his kingdom. What was his name? סיחון was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how the names work. It agrees that all three names refer to the same king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree only about which name is the nickname and which is the real name. Both agree he is one person, so the answer to step 4 holds either way.

phrases.english: Some say:
Arad, because he resembled a wild donkey in the desert;
Canaan, after his kingdom;
and what was his name? Sihon was his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternate version of the ברייתא from step 5, reaching the same result.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still one king; his real name is סיחון.

steps.title: Perhaps the new year begins in אייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether the year really starts in ניסן; maybe it starts in אייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the new year is in אייר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It is setting up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the proof shows only that אב and the following שבט are in the same year. That fits a year starting in ניסן, but it also fits a year starting in אייר. So the גמרא has not yet proven that ניסן specifically is ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the new year, the start of the count
the month of אייר, after ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: This does not deny the proof from steps 1-6. It accepts that אב and שבט are in one year and asks only which month begins that year.

phrases.english: But say the New Year is Iyar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the timeline, the גמרא questions whether that timeline proves ניסן specifically.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the count of years from יציאת מצרים begins in ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ניסן and אייר come before אב, so the proof fits either one.

steps.title: Two פסוקים about the משכן show the year does not start in אייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אייר as the new year. The תורה calls both ניסן and the אייר right after it 'the second year', so no new year started in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be! It is written: 'In the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, the משכן was set up.' And it is written: 'In the second year, in the second month, the cloud rose from over the משכן.' The פסוק talks about ניסן and calls it 'second year'. Then it talks about אייר and still calls it 'second year'. This proves the new year is not in אייר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7 (maybe the year starts in אייר?) by bringing two פסוקים that disprove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the year started in אייר, then ניסן would belong to one year and the next אייר to the following year. But the תורה calls both of them 'the second year'. So no new year began on the first of אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
The cloud rose up (the signal to travel)
It is standing at / talking about

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it is written: 'And it was in the first month, in the second year,
on the first of the month, the Tabernacle was set up' (Shemos 40:17),
and it is written: 'And it was in the second year, in the second month,
the cloud rose up from over the Tabernacle of Testimony' (Bamidbar 10:11).
Since when it speaks of Nisan it calls it 'the second year',
and when it speaks of Iyar it also calls it 'the second year' —

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָאו אִיָּיר הוּא!
phrases.english: this shows that the new year is not Iyar!
phrases.notes: If the year had changed in אייר, the second פסוק would have said 'third year'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by disproving אייר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the new year for counting is the first of אייר.
steps.terutzMaskana: ניסן and the following אייר are in the same year, so the year does not start in אייר.

steps.title: Maybe the year starts in סיון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that maybe the new year is in סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the new year is in סיון?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that אייר is ruled out, the גמרא tries the next month, סיון. This sets up the next proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן verses only show that ניסן and אייר share a year. They say nothing about whether a new year could begin later, in סיון.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead; maybe it is
The third month, counting from ניסן

phrases.english: But say the new year is Sivan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the challenge one month later, after אייר was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the counting year begins in ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof so far only excludes אייר, so סיון is still possible.

steps.title: The פסוק about arriving at סיני shows the year does not start in סיון
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about reaching סיני in the third month does not say 'second year'. So no new year began in סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be! It is written: 'In the third month after בני ישראל left מצרים.' If the year started in סיון, the פסוק should have said: 'In the third month, in the second year after they left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects סיון by showing that the תורה would have worded the פסוק differently if a new year started then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני ישראל left מצרים in ניסן. If a new year began on the first of סיון, then by the time they reached סיני in סיון they would already be in the second year. Since the פסוק does not mention a 'second year', סיון cannot be the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: After בני ישראל went out (of מצרים)

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it is written: 'In the third month
after the children of Israel went out of the land of Egypt' (Shemos 19:1),
and if it were so (that the year starts in Sivan) —
'In the third month, in the second year after they went out, etc.'
is what it should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סיון suggestion of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disproof from the wording the פסוק should have used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The new year might start on the first of סיון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The arrival at סיני in סיון was still in the first year, so the year does not start in סיון.

steps.title: No פסוק rules out תמוז, אב or אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that תמוז, אב and אדר are still possible new-year months, and it has no פסוק to rule them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is תמוז! Or say it is אב! Or say it is אדר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises months it cannot disprove. This shows that the whole method of ruling out months one by one does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps ruled out only the months from after אב up to שבט, plus אייר and סיון. No פסוק excludes תמוז, אב or אדר, so the proof that the year begins in ניסן falls apart. That is why the גמרא now has to look for a completely new source.
steps.whatToRemember: Proving 'ניסן' by ruling out each other month failed, because תמוז, אב and אדר could not be ruled out. Step 12 brings a new source instead.

phrases.english: But say it is Tammuz!
Or say it is Av!
Or say it is Adar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that even after steps 8 and 10, the proof is still incomplete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole derivation of ניסן from the timeline of the פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No פסוק excludes these three months, so ניסן is not proven.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר proves from שלמה's building that a reign is counted from ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a new source. 'In the second month, in the second' means the second month counted from the month the king's reign is counted from, which is ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: we learn it from here: 'He began to build in the second month, in the second, in the fourth year of his reign.' What does the extra 'second' mean? Doesn't it mean second to the month from which his reign is counted?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier method failed, רבי אלעזר offers a brand-new proof that a king's years start in ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'in the second month', so the extra word 'in the second' seems unnecessary. רבי אלעזר explains that it means this month was second in the count of the king's reign. That tells us the reign is counted from the first month, ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: From which they count his reign

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: the extra 'בשני' in דברי הימים shows that a king's years are counted from ניסן.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בחודש השני' and 'בשני' are not a repetition. The first names the calendar month (אייר). The second tells us that month is second in counting the king's reign.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the new foundation for the משנה's rule that ניסן is the new year for kings.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said: it is learned from here:
'And he began to build in the second month,
in the second, in the fourth year of his reign' (Divrei HaYamim II 3:2).
What is meant by (the extra) 'second'?
Doesn't it mean second to the month
from which they count his reign?!
phrases.notes: So the reign is counted from the first month, ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed derivation (step 11) with a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king's reign is counted from ניסן, as shown by the extra word 'בשני'.

steps.title: רבינא asks: maybe the second 'second' means the second day of the month
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבי אלעזר: maybe the second 'בשני' in the פסוק means the second day of the month, not the second month counted from the month the king's reign is counted from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: But say it means 'the second of the month'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רבי אלעזר's reading of the extra word 'בשני'. He offers another way to read it: the second day of the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read 'בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי בַּשֵּׁנִי' as 'the second month, counted from the month the reign is counted from' (ניסן). רבינא says the extra 'בשני' could simply give the date: the second day of that month. If he is right, the פסוק teaches nothing about when kings' years begin.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it. This introduces a sharp challenge.
But say instead. This offers another possible reading.
The second day of the month

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objects to this:
But say: the second of the month!
phrases.notes: The word 'בַּשֵּׁנִי' in the verse would then mean the date, the second day of the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא: וְאֵימָא שֵׁנִי בַּחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבי אלעזר read the פסוק in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading of the second 'בשני' as counting from ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word can be read more simply as a day of the month, which removes the proof.

steps.title: If it meant a day of the month, the verse would say so plainly
steps.stepSummary: The reading is rejected. If the פסוק meant the second day of the month, it would have written 'שני בחדש' clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, 'the second of the month' would have been written in it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבינא's suggestion. When the פסוק wants to give a day of the month, it says so clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנ"ך normally marks a date with a clear phrase that mentions the month, such as 'on the second of the month'. Here the פסוק just says 'בשני', so it is not giving a date. That leaves room for רבי אלעזר's reading.

phrases.english: If so,
"the second of the month" would have been written in it explicitly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, שֵׁנִי בַּחֹדֶשׁ בְּהֶדְיָא הֲוָה כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument from how the פסוק is worded
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בשני' might just be the date in the month.
steps.terutzMaskana: A date would be written clearly as 'שני בחדש'. So 'בשני' means something else.

steps.title: Maybe it means the second day of the week
steps.stepSummary: A new suggestion: maybe 'בשני' means Monday, the second day of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: on the second day of the week!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another way to read 'בשני'. It could mean the second day of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day-of-the-month reading was rejected. Now the extra word might name the weekday on which the building began. If so, it again says nothing about when kings' years begin.

keyTerms.meaning: The second day of the week (Monday)
Here it means 'week', not the day of שבת itself.

phrases.english: But say: on the second day of the week!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the day-of-the-month reading is rejected, a second other reading is offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'בשני' could name the weekday, which again removes the proof.

steps.title: Two reasons it cannot mean the day of the week
steps.stepSummary: Two answers. תנ"ך never dates events by the day of the week. Also, the two 'שני's in the פסוק are compared, so both mean a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, we have never found 'the second day of the week' written. And further, the verse compares the later 'second' to the first 'second'. Just as the first 'second' is a month, so too the later 'second' is a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the day-of-the-week reading with two separate reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1: תנ"ך never tells us the weekday on which something happened, so this would be a strange exception. Reason 2: the two 'second's sit right next to each other and should be read the same way. The first one clearly means the second month, so the second one also counts months. That is exactly רבי אלעזר's reading: the second month counted from ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: And further. This adds a second reason.
It compares or links one thing to another

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's reading stands. 'בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי בַּשֵּׁנִי' means the second month counted from the month that reigns are counted from, which is ניסן.

phrases.english: First, that we have not found
"the second day of the week" written anywhere.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: מַקִּישׁ שֵׁנִי בָּתְרָא לְשֵׁנִי קַמָּא:
phrases.english: And further: it compares the later "second" to the first "second":
just as the first "second" is a month,
so too the later "second" is a month.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא, דְּלָא אַשְׁכְּחַן שֵׁנִי בַּשַּׁבָּת דִּכְתִיב. וְעוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 and ends the defense of רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two reasons: how תנ"ך usually dates events, and a comparison between the two words in the same פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: תנ"ך never dates by weekday, and the two 'second's are compared, so both mean a month.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: the first set of verses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs רבי יוחנן's rule that kings' years are counted only from ניסן. It starts by listing פסוקים: the date of the בית המקדש, the death of אהרן, and משה's speech in the eleventh month of the fortieth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that kings' years are counted only from ניסן? As it says: 'And it was in the four hundred and eightieth year after בני ישראל left מצרים...' And it is written: 'And אהרן הכהן went up to הר ההר at the word of ה׳...' And it is written: 'And it was in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא begins collecting the פסוקים it needs; the proof itself has not been made yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lines up dates. The first פסוק ties שלמה's reign to the count from יציאת מצרים. אהרן died in the fortieth year, in the fifth month (אב). משה spoke in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month (שבט). Since אב and the later שבט are both 'the fortieth year', no new year started between them. The remaining פסוקים in the next steps narrow it down to ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him
We count the years of kings

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא often quotes only the opening words of a פסוק and ends with 'וגו׳'. The words it actually needs are often in the part it left out. For example, 'the fortieth year, in the fifth month' is in the unquoted part of the פסוק about אהרן.

phrases.english: It is taught in a Baraita in agreement with Rabbi Yochanan:
From where do we know that we do not count years for kings
except from Nisan?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בִשְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה

phrases.notes: מלכים א ו:א. The building of the בית המקדש, which the פסוק says began in 'the second month'.

phrases.aramaic: לְצֵאת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: after the children of Israel left the land of Egypt, etc."

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַל אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אֶל הֹר הָהָר
phrases.english: And it is written: "And Aaron the priest went up to Mount Hor
phrases.notes: במדבר לג:לח. אהרן died in the fortieth year, in the fifth month (אב).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי אלעזר to a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that kings' years are counted only from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא built on a chain of פסוקים about the fortieth year in the desert

steps.title: The ברייתא adds פסוקים about סיחון, the כנעני, and the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its chain. משה spoke after סיחון was defeated. The כנעני attacked after hearing that אהרן died. The nation saw that אהרן died. And the משכן was set up in the first month of the second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'After he struck סיחון...' And it says: 'And the כנעני heard...' And it says: 'And all the congregation saw that אהרן had died...' And it says: 'And it was in the first month in the second year...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps adding the pieces it needs to build its proof. It never states the conclusion in words. The list itself sums up the proof the גמרא worked through earlier on this amud, and the list ends in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים set the order of events. אהרן died first. Then the כנעני, who is סיחון (steps 5–6), heard and attacked, and he was defeated. Only after that did משה speak in the eleventh month. The last פסוק ('the first month in the second year', when the משכן was set up) begins the step-by-step check of which month starts the year. It pairs with the אייר פסוק in the next step to rule out אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Canaanite, the king of Arad
And it says. This adds another פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: The order of events is the core of the proof. Events in אב and in the later שבט are both called 'the fortieth year', so no new year began in any month from אלול through שבט (including תשרי). On its own this does not prove ניסן. The later פסוקים rule out אייר and סיון, and רבי אלעזר's 'ויחל לבנות' closes the gap of תמוז, אב and אדר (steps 11–12).

phrases.english: And it is written: "After he struck Sichon, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים א:ד. משה's speech came after סיחון was defeated.

phrases.english: And it says: "And the Canaanite heard, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר לג:מ. He heard that אהרן died and came to attack.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וַיִּרְאוּ כׇּל הָעֵדָה כִּי גָוַע אַהֲרֹן וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: And it says: "And all the congregation saw that Aaron had died, etc."
And it says: "And it was in the first month
phrases.notes: שמות מ:יז. The משכן was set up.

phrases.english: in the second year, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by adding more פסוקים to the chain.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that kings' years are counted only from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of events: אהרן's death, the כנעני's attack, the war with סיחון, משה's speech, and the setting up of the משכן

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes its list of proof verses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its chain with three more פסוקים: the second month of the second year, the third month after leaving מצרים, and שלמה beginning to build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month…' And it says: 'In the third month after בני ישראל went out…' And it says: 'And he began to build…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes listing the פסוקים that together build רבי יוחנן's proof. This closes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These verses repeat the steps of the גמרא's discussion. The second-month verse, read with the משכן verse, rules out אייר (step 8). The third-month verse rules out סיון (step 10). The last verse, 'ויחל לבנות,' is רבי אלעזר's source (step 12). It closes the gap left by תמוז, אב and אדר, and directly shows that a king's reign is counted from ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says' — introduces the next פסוק in a chain of proofs
'Etc.' — the rest of the פסוק is assumed to be known
'And he began to build' — שלמה starting the בית המקדש
After the Jewish people left מצרים

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is now complete. Its point is that a Jewish king's years are counted from ניסן, the same way the years from יציאת מצרים are counted.

phrases.english: And it says: 'And it came to pass in the second year,
in the second month, etc.'
And it says: 'In the third month
after the children of Israel went out, etc.'
And it says: 'And he began to build, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב ג:ב — שלמה building the בית המקדש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the ברייתא's chain of פסוקים from steps 17-18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that kings' years are counted from ניסן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing פסוקים from במדבר, שמות, and דברי הימים

steps.title: Non-Jewish kings count their years from תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the ניסן rule applies only to Jewish kings. Kings of other nations count from תשרי. He brings two פסוקים from נחמיה as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They taught this only about the kings of Israel. But for the kings of the nations of the world, we count from תשרי. As it says: 'The words of נחמיה son of חכליה: It happened in the month of כסלו, in the twentieth year…' And it is written: 'It happened in the month of ניסן, in the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא limits the rule we just learned. Only מלכי ישראל count from ניסן; non-Jewish kings count from תשרי. He quotes two פסוקים to set up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we assumed every king's years start in ניסן. רב חסדא narrows the rule and gives מלכי אומות העולם a different start, תשרי. The two פסוקים from נחמיה are the raw material for the proof, which is spelled out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about…' — limits an earlier rule
A Persian king (Artaxerxes) in whose court נחמיה served

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two different 'new years' for counting kings. The rest of the sugya tests whether the proof for this split holds up.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only regarding the kings of Israel,
but for the kings of the nations of the world —
we count from Tishrei,
as it is said: 'The words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah:

phrases.aramaic: וַיְהִי בְחֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵיו שְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: It happened in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, etc.'
And it is written: 'It happened in the month of Nisan,
in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא's ניסן rule and limits it to Jewish kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewish kings count their years from ניסן; non-Jewish kings count from תשרי.

steps.title: כסלו and the following ניסן share the same year
steps.stepSummary: Both כסלו and the ניסן that comes after it are called 'the twentieth year.' So the year did not start over in ניסן, and for this king the new year cannot be ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק stands in כסלו and calls it 'the twentieth year,' and stands in ניסן and still calls it 'the twentieth year,' this shows that the new year is not ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two פסוקים prove רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כסלו comes before ניסן. If the year started over in ניסן, that ניסן would be the twenty-first year. Since it is still called the twentieth year, the year must turn over at a different point, which is תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since it stands at' — the timing the פסוק is speaking about
'This shows that' — introduces a conclusion drawn by inference

steps.confusionAlert: The ניסן in the second פסוק comes AFTER the כסלו, a few months later in time. That is the whole point: no new year started in between.

phrases.english: Since when it stands in Kislev
it calls it 'the twentieth year,'
and when it stands in Nisan
it still calls it 'the twentieth year' —

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָאו נִיסָן הוּא.
phrases.english: this shows that the new year is not Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the פסוקים quoted in step 20 prove רב חסדא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that non-Jewish kings count from תשרי

steps.title: How do we know the כסלו פסוק counts ארתחשסתא's years
steps.stepSummary: The ניסן פסוק clearly says 'of ארתחשסתא,' but the כסלו פסוק does not. Maybe its 'twentieth year' counts something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, that one explicitly says it is of ארתחשסתא. But this one, how do we know it is of ארתחשסתא? Perhaps…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's proof. This passage stops in the middle of the challenge, and the 'perhaps' continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if both פסוקים count the same king's years. Only the ניסן verse names ארתחשסתא. If the כסלו verse uses a different count, then the two 'twentieth years' have nothing to do with each other, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted' — accepts one point before attacking another

phrases.english: Granted, that one [the Nisan verse] —
it is explicit that it refers to Artaxerxes,
but this one [the Kislev verse] —
from where do we know it refers to Artaxerxes?
Perhaps…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof built in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's proof from the two נחמיה פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof assumes both פסוקים count ארתחשסתא's years, but only one of them says so. The כסלו verse may be using a different count.
